items.title: Sarawak needs more dietitians to promote balanced nutrition, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 4 — Sarawak needs more professional dietetic experts to ensure balanced meals in daily nutrition, said Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. He said that the presence of professional dietitians is important to help the community understand the nutritional content of food and to plan meals that meet dietary needs. “We need many professional dietetic experts so that the food we serve is balanced from a dietary perspective.

items.title: Five immigration officers remanded over alleged role in MyIMMs hacking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Five Immigration Department officers have been remanded until Aug 6 to assist investigations into their alleged involvement in the hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs), linked to the unlawful processing and approval of Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS). Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order against the four men and one woman, aged between their 30s and 40s, at the Putrajaya Magistrate's Court today following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).S MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Mukhriz’s challenge against RM5m IRB tax notices gets Nov 16 decision date
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The High Court today fixed Nov 16 to deliver its decision on a judicial review application filed by Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir challenging the Inland Revenue Board's (IRB) issuance of Notices of Additional Assessment totalling more than RM5 million for the 2017 to 2019 assessment years. Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad set the date after hearing submissions from lawyer Nizamuddin Abdul Hamid, representing Mukhriz, and Senior Revenue Counsel Marina Ibrahim, appearing for the Director-General of the Inland Revenue Board. On Jan 2, 2025, the High Court granted Mukhriz leave to commence the judicial review proceedings.

items.title: Foreign Ministry tracking 21,427 Malaysians in conflict-hit countries for possible evacuation
items.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said experience in handling previous conflicts had helped the government strengthen its preparedness. Lukanisman said Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) also had its own plan to evacuate its employees. Responding to Musoddak’s original question on the plan to protect Malaysians in the Middle East, including Umrah pilgrims, Lukanisman said all Malaysian diplomatic missions have a contingency plan that is constantly updated, including mapping the location of Malaysians, communication mechanisms, resource coordination and evacuation strategies.

items.title: Former plantation manager held over RM8m rubber seedling contracts probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a former plantation manager of a rubber seedling supplier in the Klang Valley over alleged misappropriation involving contracts worth about RM8 million. The man, in his 50s, is being investigated over allegations of abusing contracts for the supply of rubber seedlings to subsidiaries of a statutory body involved in the plantation sector. According to an MACC source, the suspect was arrested at about 7pm yesterday after he turned up at the MACC headquarters to have his statement recorded.

items.title: Perak Sultan opens Manjung Municipal Council’s new Merdeka Hall
items.summary: LUMUT, Aug 4 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today opened the Merdeka Hall of the Manjung Municipal Council here. The Raja Permaisuri of Perak, Tuanku Zara Salim, and the Raja Di Hilir of Perak, Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah also attended the event. In his speech, Saarani said the opening of the hall marked three closely linked milestones.

items.title: MACC nabs director in RM300,000 Tabung Haji bribery probes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a company director for allegedly bribing a former chief operating officer (COO) of a statutory body with renovation works worth about RM300,000 in return for securing renovation contracts. The arrest followed investigations by a special task force set up to review the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji. The RCI report was made public on July 29 through the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim)'s official portal.

items.title: Building facade collapses in Penang, two injured
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Two people are believed to have been injured after the facade of a building along Lebuh Armenian here collapsed on them. Lebuh Armenian is a narrow street in George Town, located within the city's Unesco World Heritage Site. Renowned for its vibrant cultural heritage and captivating street art, it has become one of George Town's most popular attractions.

items.title: Oil giant Aramco's profits soar 44 pct as war boosts prices
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi Aramco on Tuesday said its net profit rose 44 per cent in the second quarter year-on-year as the Middle East war pushed oil and gas prices higher. Aramco, majority-owned by the state, reported net income of 122.6 billion Saudi riyals ($32.7 billion) from April to June, up from 85 billion riyals ($22.67 billion) in 2025. Stripping out exceptional items, adjusted net income came in at 125.1 billion Saudi riyals ($33.4 billion).

items.title: Police arrest three after missing Johor man found dead in river
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 4 — Police have arrested three men to assist in the investigation into the discovery of a man’s body in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, Batu Pahat, yesterday. Deputy Johor police chief Hoo Chuan Huat said the victim was found wrapped in a fishing net, with his hands and feet tied with adhesive tape and injuries on his body. He said the discovery of the victim’s body was reported by the public at 12.30pm yesterday.

items.title: Inflation back in focus as energy prices reshape market outlook, says JustMarkets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Inflation has re-emerged as a key driver of global financial markets in 2026 as higher energy prices, uncertain central bank policy and slowing economic growth reshape investor expectations, trading platform JustMarkets said. The firm said upcoming consumer price index (CPI) data will be closely watched as markets gauge the outlook for interest rates, currencies, bond yields and risk assets. Conversely, weaker inflation data could strengthen expectations for monetary easing, lifting investor sentiment and supporting risk assets.

items.title: MCW urges focus on KLIA security lapses in pilot drug probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Corruption Watch (MCW) has called for investigations into the arrest of a pilot found with drugs in Indonesia to focus on potential weaknesses in security systems at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), rather than solely identifying which agency was responsible. Its president, Jais Abdul Karim, said the statement by the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) that the pilot had cleared all security checks at KLIA, while baggage screening fell under Aviation Security (AVSEC), should be viewed in its entirety. "The real issue is how such a large quantity of drugs could allegedly pass through the security system of an international airport.

items.title: Madani economy framework's biggest challenge now is stronger execution, not policy direction: Economist
items.summary: BANGI: The Madani Economy framework has made progress in several key areas but stronger execution and better public reporting are needed to achieve its aspirations. "Looking more specifically, when the framework was launched, it outlined seven medium- and long-term aspirations under the Madani Economy. The panel session was held as the Madani Economy framework marked three years since its launch by the government on July 27, 2023.

items.title: AI training using copyrighted works requires owners’ approval, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The use of copyrighted material for artificial intelligence (AI) model training is subject to approval from copyright holders, with licensing arrangements and royalty payments to be agreed by the relevant parties under the Copyright Act 1987. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh said the requirement applies to any use of copyrighted works, whether for AI applications or other purposes. Fuziah said Section 27 of the Copyright Act 1987 stipulates that payment arrangements are subject to agreements between parties, which can be carried out through licensing, rights assignments or managed through Collective Management Organisations (CMOs) representing copyright owners.

items.title: Motac supports bringing international artists for Sepang F1 after-party
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (Motac) will support efforts to bring international artists to Malaysia for the Formula 1 after-party, said its secretary-general Datuk Shaharuddin Abu Sohot. He said that while such entertainment programmes are typically organised by the private sector, the ministry plays a role in supporting and promoting them. "We do encourage and help promote international programmes that come to our country," he told reporters on the sidelines of the 11th Malaysia Business Events Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.

items.title: Malaysia's physical rice stocks sufficient for six months
items.summary: Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the current inventory stands at 1.237 million tonnes, comprising 200,000 tonnes in national buffer stock and 1.037 million tonnes in commercial reserves. "We maintain the physical rice buffer stock managed by Padiberas Nasional Bhd (Bernas), as well as commercial stocks that can last at least six months in the event of an impending global supply crisis," he said during Question Time. Chan added that the supply control mechanism is supported by government subsidies to regulate local white rice prices, ensuring market stability when global commodity prices fluctuate.

items.title: Three Bangladeshis killed, one injured in suspected fight among co-workers
items.summary: Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police also arrested a fellow Bangladeshi man in his 40s who is believed to be involved in the incident. He said police received a report from members of the public at about 4.15pm yesterday about a fight involving several Bangladeshi nationals at the house. Alzafny said preliminary investigations later led police to the discovery of two more bodies at the Sua Manggis estate in Linggi.

items.title: Drug seizures at KLIA jump nearly six-fold as syndicates target airport
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 4 — Federal narcotics police said today that drug syndicates may be favouring Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) as a transit hub because flights from the airport are not prioritised for security screening over those from other regional airports. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, however, said the number of arrests and drug seizures indicated that KLIA remained a preferred transit point for syndicates attempting to smuggle drugs overseas. “The estimated value of the drugs seized in 2026 is RM108.35 million, compared with RM18.46 million last year,” he said.

items.title: Child sexual abuse cases in Selangor surge 70pc since 2021
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Child sexual abuse cases in Selangor have increased by 70 per cent since 2021, the state assembly was told today. This was followed by physical abuse (1,654 cases), non-physical abuse (156), possession of child pornography (42), and producing or distributing child pornography (24). NST, News, Malaysia News, Selangor, child sexual abuse, sexual crimes, Anfaal Saari, state assembly, rape cases, physical sexual abuse, child protection, Talian Kasih 15999 © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: GFM wins RM83.1mil Pengerang contracts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Integrated facilities management services provider GFM Services Bhd has secured additional release orders worth RM83.1 million for major turnaround works at the Pengerang Integrated Complex (PIC) in Johor. The contracts comprise RM16.3 million awarded to its wholly-owned subsidiary Highbase Strategic Sdn Bhd by Petronas Chemicals Isononanol Sdn Bhd and RM66.8 million awarded to its 60 per cent-owned indirect subsidiary Shapadu CR Asia Sdn Bhd by Pengerang Refining Company Sdn Bhd. Including the RM148.2 million in release orders secured in July, GFM has accumulated turnaround work packages at PIC worth RM231.3 million.

items.title: Family of sisters killed in Klang crash considers legal action
items.summary: KLANG: The family of two sisters killed in a fatal accident is considering legal action against the accused, the lawyer representing their interests said. Tan said this after mention proceedings for Ang Kim Lai, 75, who pleaded not guilty to a charge of reckless driving that allegedly caused the deaths of Wong Nyok Sim, 61, and Wong Nyoke Fong, 56. The offence allegedly took place at 7.30pm on May 15 along Jalan Pekan Baru.

items.title: Toyota lifts annual forecast despite Q1 profit drop on weak China sales
items.summary: TOKYO: Toyota on Tuesday raised its annual operating profit forecast by 13 per cent to reflect a weaker yen — the upward revision coming despite reporting a fifth consecutive quarterly earnings decrease on slumping sales in China. The world's largest automaker now expects 3.4 trillion yen (US$21.6 billion) in operating profit for the current financial year to end-March, up from its previous forecast of three trillion yen. Operating profit for the April-June first quarter declined nine per cent to 1.06 trillion yen, compared with a median forecast of 1.11 trillion yen in a poll of eight analysts surveyed by LSEG.

items.title: Toyota profit drops for fifth straight quarter on China slump, Iran war impact
items.summary: TOKYO: Toyota said on Tuesday that profit fell for a fifth straight quarter, hurt by a slide in China sales as well as higher material and parts costs stemming from the Iran war. Operating profit for the April-June first quarter declined nine per cent to 1.06 trillion yen (US$6.7 billion), compared with a median forecast of 1.11 trillion yen in a poll of eight analysts surveyed by LSEG. But the world's largest automaker lifted its full-year profit outlook by 13 per cent to 3.4 trillion yen from 3.0 trillion yen.

items.title: 2 who died in Japan mall explosion were told by employer to return inside
items.summary: TOKYO: Two women who died in an explosion at an Aeon shopping mall in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, had originally safely evacuated following a major earthquake but were ordered back inside to secure cash, Xinhua reported. After Tuesday's magnitude 7.1 earthquake, which registered up to 7, the highest level on Japan's seismic intensity scale, a massive explosion ripped through the Aeon Mall Kumamoto building in Kashima Town, killing seven people, including the two employees. The two, including a 22-year-old woman, had initially evacuated the mall after the powerful quake, but were told to return inside to put cash in a safe.

items.title: Hartalega's Q1 earnings jump on higher prices, cost savings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hartalega Holdings Bhd's net profit surged to RM70 million in the first quarter ended June 30 2026 from RM12.6 million a year ago. Hartalega said it remains cautiously optimistic about the long-term outlook for the global glove industry. Hartalega said near-term operating conditions are expected to remain challenging as continued uncertainty over US tariff policies reshapes global trade flows.

items.title: Hotel worker gets five years' jail, whipping for sexually assaulting fiancée's daughter
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A hotel worker was sentenced to five years' jail and two strokes of the rotan by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two counts of sexually assaulting his fiancée's 16-year-old daughter at a hotel in Tanah Merah last month. The 34-year-old accused entered the guilty plea after the charges were read before judge Zulkpli Abdullah. The accused was charged with sexually assaulting the teenager at 3am and 11am in a hotel room in Tanah Merah on July 24.

items.title: Radzi Rahimi remembered as a dedicated leader who inspired Maran youth, says Pahang MB
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The tragic death of Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi is a huge loss to the community in Maran, especially its youth, as he had devoted much of his time to serving the people. Pahang Menteri Besar and Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail described Radzi as an approachable leader who was respected by people from all walks of life and remembered for his cheerful personality. Meanwhile, Maran Umno division chief Datuk Seri Shahaniza Shamsuddin said she was very close to Radzi and knew the late leader was well-liked by people from all walks of life, especially the youth in Maran.

items.title: Op Kalidasa cripples syndicate, RM20.74 million in drugs seized
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police have crippled a drug trafficking syndicate after seizing 409.4kg of methamphetamine and 900 MDMA-laced vape cartridges worth a combined RM20.74 million in Selangor. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said two local men, aged 24 and 26, were arrested in two raids under Op Kalidasa on July 29. He said police caught the two suspects while they were unloading sacks believed to contain drugs into two Proton X70 vehicles.

items.title: Guatemala issues 'danger' alert after Fuego volcano erupts
items.summary: Guatemala City, (GUATEMALA): Guatemalan authorities issued on Monday the country's second-highest emergency alert level after a major eruption of Central America's most active volcano. "An orange (danger) alert has been declared nationwide due to the eruption of the Fuego volcano," said disaster coordination agency Conred on X as it began evacuating two villages near the volcano, located 35 kilometers (22 miles) from capital Guatemala City. Another eruption in 2023 from the 3,763-meter (12,346-foot) Fuego caused the evacuation of around 1,200 people.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin opens Dewan Merdeka as Manjung eyes Tourism, Maritime City status
items.summary: LUMUT: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today officially opened the Manjung Municipal Council's Dewan Merdeka, marking a significant milestone in the district's transformation towards becoming a Tourism and Maritime City by 2030. Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim; Raja Di Hilir of Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah; Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad; and Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. In his speech, Saarani said Manjung was steadily positioning itself as a Tourism and Maritime City by 2030, with good governance, strategic investments and sustainable development forming the foundation of its transformation.

items.title: Govt mulls registry to monitor repeat domestic violence offenders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying a proposal to establish a Domestic Violence Offenders Registry to monitor repeat offenders, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said. "The ministry remains committed to tackling domestic violence through a comprehensive whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach," she said during Question Time in the Dewan Negara today. Meanwhile, she said the ministry has allocated RM2.1 million this year to upgrade more than 20 government-run shelters for domestic violence victims nationwide.

items.title: Three detained for trespassing in restricted zone beneath Penang Bridge
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Three people were detained for allegedly trespassing into a restricted area beneath the Penang Bridge during a maritime enforcement operation. Penang Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Maritime Captain Muhammad Suffi Mohd Ramli said the arrests were made at 1.30pm yesterday during a routine patrol in Penang waters. He said inspections at the bridge pillar area found two men and a woman within the Gazetted Restricted Area without authorisation.

items.title: How did a Malaysia Airlines pilot’s drug-filled baggage clear KLIA? Police identify person of interest
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 4 — Federal police said today they have identified a person of interest in their investigation into how a Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at an Indonesian airport passed through security screening at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) without his baggage being flagged. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the person of interest is an airport employee in his 30s who was assigned to the security screening area through which the pilot passed. Citing Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, Hussein said the pilot’s baggage was not flagged as high risk and was cleared under existing standard operating procedures without undergoing a secondary inspection.

items.title: Forest fire spreads in Dutch nature reserve
items.summary: THE HAGUE: Firefighters are rushing to contain a forest blaze in the southeast of the Netherlands that spread overnight to engulf 100 hectares on Tuesday, authorities said. The blaze spread to 100 hectares as of early Tuesday and was still not under control, provincial authorities said on their website. "Because of the drought, fire can spread quickly in nature reserves," the provincial authorities said, without specifying the cause of the fire.

items.title: [UPDATED] KLIA to prioritise drug detection in baggage screening after high-level security meeting
items.summary: Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the meeting agreed that KLIA's existing screening system, which has traditionally focused on detecting firearms, explosives and other aviation security threats, should also place greater emphasis on narcotics detection. Hussein said KLIA's security system involved multiple screening levels, beginning with automated scans using airport screening equipment. He said investigations showed the pilot had undergone all required security screening procedures at KLIA, including the first-level baggage screening.

items.title: Govt eyes levy on EVs to close gap in public charging infrastructure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The government is considering imposing a levy on every electric vehicle (EV) sold to establish a fund for expanding Malaysia’s public EV charging network, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said. Johari said the government had previously granted exemptions on import duty, excise duty and sales tax for completely built-up (CBU) EVs for four years to spur market growth and attract investment. “After four years, when we looked for public charging stations, the investment from EV industry players was simply not there,” he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Op Khas KLIA nets 13 drug mules, RM21.3mil in drugs seized
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police arrested 13 suspected drug mules and seized cannabis buds and cocaine worth RM21.3 million in the latest Op Khas KLIA drug bust. "Those arrested comprised three local men, two local women, six foreign men and two foreign women. Police seized 260.08kg of cannabis buds and 1.01kg of cocaine.

items.title: [UPDATED] KLIA-linked drug seizures surge nearly six-fold to RM108mil
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said 1,353.41kg of drugs were seized between January and July this year, compared with 235.36kg seized during the corresponding period last year. "The value of the drugs seized also increased sharply from RM18.46 million in 2025 to RM108.35 million this year. Hussein said arrests increased from 57 individuals last year to 121 this year.

items.title: Denmark targets August 21 for second Security Council UN chief poll
items.summary: NEW YORK: The United Nations Security Council is expected to hold another informal poll this month as it selects the next UN secretary-general, the council president for August said on Monday, while indicating that a decision is still some way off. That showed former Costa Rican Vice President Rebeca Grynspan as a narrow early frontrunner among seven current candidates, followed by former Guyanese Foreign Minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett and then Argentina's Rafael Grossi, head of the UN nuclear watchdog. The other current candidates are former Chilean President Michelle Bachelet, former Ecuadorean Foreign Minister Maria Fernanda Espinosa, former Senegalese President Macky Sall, and Ugandan diplomat Olara Otunnu.

items.title: Sabah proposes tourism be placed under Concurrent List in line with MA63
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 4 — The Sabah state government has proposed for tourism to be placed under the Concurrent List of the Federal Constitution, in line with the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63). State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the proposal is not intended to separate Sabah from the national tourism framework, but rather to establish a more effective operational partnership between the federal and state governments. “Sabah’s unique biodiversity, extensive protected areas, island tourism, and indigenous heritage require tailored policies that address the state’s specific geographical and socio-economic realities,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Mother’s desperate attempts to save son fail in Kuala Terengganu fire
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 4 — A mother was overcome with regret after failing to save her son who was trapped in a fire that destroyed their home in here last night. Sharipah Yusof, 59, said she tried three times to brave the flames and enter the house to rescue her son, Abd Latif Abd Rashid, 41, who was sleeping in a locked room upstairs when the incident occurred at 10.52 pm. “The person told us the house was on fire and pulled us out.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan considers creating Deputy Exco positions, says MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 4 — The Negeri Sembilan government is considering a proposal to create Deputy Executive Council (Exco) positions for several portfolios as part of efforts to strengthen the state administration, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. He said Exco positions would be filled by several state assemblymen from Barisan Nasional (BN) component parties, PAS and Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan). “There may not be enough Exco posts to offer, so we are considering creating Deputy Exco positions for several portfolios that I believe are important,” he told reporters at Wisma Negeri here today.

items.title: Suhakam: Further delay in Pastor Raymond Koh case could jeopardise crucial evidence, witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) today warned that the Court of Appeal’s decision last week to keep parts of the High Court’s ruling in Pastor Raymond Koh’s disappearance case on hold could further delay the search for truth and accountability. In November 2025, the High Court found the government and police liable for Koh’s enforced disappearance and ordered the investigation to be reopened under several conditions. Suhakam’s 2019 public inquiry had earlier concluded that Koh, who disappeared in February 2017, was the victim of an enforced disappearance carried out by state agents.

items.title: Teenage students killed after motorcycle crashes near Temerloh
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 4 — Two 17-year-old school students were killed in a three-vehicle crash at KM119 of Jalan Kuala Lumpur-Kuantan near Temerloh yesterday. Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police were alerted to the crash involving a motorcyclist and his pillion rider at 8.20 pm. He said initial investigations indicated the victims were travelling from Temerloh town towards Chenor in Maran at the time of the crash.

items.title: Pulau Burung landfill fire extinguished after nearly four-hour operation
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Aug 4 — The Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) took nearly four hours to fully extinguish a landfill fire at the Pulau Burung Solid Waste Disposal Site here last night. Its Fire and Rescue Operations Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said a team from the Nibong Tebal Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) was sent to the scene after receiving an emergency call at 8.14 pm. The fire involved an area measuring 120 feet by 90 feet, with the operation commander conducting an initial assessment before directing firefighters to contain and extinguish the blaze, including building a fire break to prevent it from spreading.

items.title: MACC arrests five more immigration officers over alleged MyIMMs hacking
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 4 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested five more immigration officers for allegedly colluding in hacking the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to facilitate the unlawful processing and approval of Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS). “Following the arrests, the MACC seized five mobile phones belonging to the suspects,” the source said. On July 28, the MACC arrested 12 individuals, including six immigration officers, in a joint operation conducted with several other agencies across the Klang Valley and Penang.

items.title: Anwar praises Malaysian contingent’s fighting spirit at Glasgow Commonwealth Games
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated the entire Malaysian contingent for their fighting spirit and commendable performances at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games. In a Facebook post last night, he also expressed appreciation to the coaches, officials, support staff and all Malaysians who continuously prayed for the success of the national contingent. “Alhamdulillah, my heartfelt congratulations to the entire Malaysian contingent for competing with great pride and displaying extraordinary fighting spirit at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Govt seeks wider gas supply options as Malaysia moves to boost energy security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The government is prioritising Malaysia’s energy security by diversifying access to large-scale gas resources that could broaden supply options and enhance the country’s energy resilience. The Economy Ministry said that amid uncertainty in global energy markets caused by geopolitical tensions, Malaysia remained focused on diversifying its energy supply sources to reduce reliance on any single country or market. Regarding opportunities to develop gas fields in Turkmenistan, the ministry said such ventures would be assessed based on their commercial merits and potential contribution to diversifying Malaysia’s long-term gas supply.

items.title: KTMB expands Southern Shuttle route linking Paloh to JB Sentral from Aug 8
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) will extend its Southern Shuttle service on the Paloh-JB Sentral-Paloh route from Aug 8. KTMB said in a statement yesterday that the expanded service will cover seven stations—Paloh, Kluang, Renggam, Layang-Layang, Kulai, Kempas Baru and JB Sentral—with the journey from Paloh to JB Sentral taking about 120 minutes. KTMB said the new service will operate 10 trips daily, comprising five services from Paloh to JB Sentral and five in the opposite direction, with each train accommodating up to 400 passengers.

items.title: Malaysia, Cambodia to strengthen cooperation in AI, digital economy and cross-border crime, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Malaysia and Cambodia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening strategic cooperation across various sectors, including the digital economy, artificial intelligence (AI), the halal industry, food security and human capital development, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a Facebook post last night he said the commitment also encompassed efforts to enhance cooperation in combating cross-border crime. Anwar said the matter was discussed during a courtesy call by Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Prak Sokhonn, who began a two-day official visit to Malaysia today.

items.title: Loke resigns as Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman after state election defeat, stays on as party sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today announced his resignation as Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman following Saturday’s outcome of the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, in which he failed to retain the Chennah seat. ”I feel that the time has come for me to step down as state chairman and leave it to the Negeri Sembilan leadership and the Negeri Sembilan DAP committee to appoint and choose one of the existing committee members to become the new Negeri Sembilan chairman,” he said. Elaborating further, Loke said a Negeri Sembilan DAP committee meeting would be held soon to elect a new state chairman and leadership line-up.

items.title: DAP to put govt role to vote as delegates decide whether party stays until Parliament ends
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — DAP will table a motion to decide if the party will remain in the government till the end of the current Parliament’s term at its National Convention on Aug 16. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the matter was decided at the party’s central executive committee (CEC) meeting yesterday. DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo, DAP deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh and the party’s senior leadership attended the meeting.

items.title: What is a ‘new born child’? Malaysia’s Court of Appeal clarifies citizenship laws for abandoned children
items.summary: But what is a “new born child”? While agreeing that G was abandoned as a child, the court said Section 19B “does not apply to every abandoned child” as Section 19B also requires the child to also be “new born”. The court said it cannot remove the “new born” requirement from Section 19B.

items.title: Indonesian authorities put out airport video of Malaysian pilot allegedly smuggling 25kg ecstasy
items.summary: JAKARTA, Aug 3 — Indonesia’s Directorate General of Customs and Excise (Bea Cukai) has released CCTV footage showing the movements of a Malaysian pilot arrested last week over the alleged smuggling of about 25 kilogrammes of ecstasy through Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. The video, uploaded on Bea Cukai’s official Instagram account on Monday, shows the 39-year-old suspect, dressed in a pilot’s uniform, collecting a large silver hard-shell suitcase from the baggage carousel while pulling a second black suitcase before walking through the arrival hall towards the customs clearance area. Close-up footage shows customs officers examining and removing the packages from the suitcase while the suspect is questioned during the inspection.

items.title: Maran Umno Youth chief, wife and child among four killed in Bentong crash
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 3 — Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi died alongside his wife, child, and brother-in-law in a car accident in Bentong on Monday. The family was travelling in a four-wheel-drive vehicle along Jalan Lama Bentong when a massive tree collapsed, crushing the vehicle and killing four of its occupants.. “I am deeply saddened to receive news of the passing of the late Edy, Maran Umno Youth chief, together with his wife, child and brother-in-law, who were killed in an accident in Bentong.

items.title: Police question 10 individuals over deaths of two teen girls in Ipoh
items.summary: LARUT, Aug 3 — Police have recorded statements from 10 individuals to assist investigations into the deaths of two female students whose bodies were found at the Sungai Pari flats in Ipoh on July 24. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those questioned included the victims’ friends and teachers. So far, our investigation has found no evidence of foul play,” he told reporters at the Selama district police headquarters today.

items.title: MACC officer rejects bias claim in Lim Guan Eng undersea tunnel probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigating officer today denied that his investigation into the RM6.3 billion Penang undersea tunnel and major roads project involving former Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng was conducted in a biased manner. Senior Superintendent Zulhilmi Ramli, 34, of the MACC Investigation Division at its headquarters, rejected the suggestion during cross-examination by defence lawyer Mohd Haijan Omar at Lim’s corruption trial. Earlier, Mohd Haijan questioned why investigators had not verified whether Consortium Zenith Beijing Urban Construction Group (CZBUCG) had submitted any claim to the Penang government for the feasibility study and detailed design (FSDD) relating to the undersea tunnel project.

items.title: ‘Slander and forgery’: Warisan denies fake letter claiming unity government exit
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 3 — Parti Warisan (Warisan) has strongly denied a viral social media claim alleging that the party has decided to withdraw from the Unity Government. Meanwhile, Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal also confirmed that the document titled “Parti WARISAN Menarik Diri Daripada Kerajaan Perpaduan” (Parti Warisan Withdraws from the Unity Government) is fake. Mohammad Yusof stressed that any official position or decision by Warisan would only be communicated through the party’s official communication channels and authorised leaders.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines pilot’s baggage raised no alarm at KLIA before drug arrest in Jakarta, border agency chief says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Malaysian authorities are examining how a pilot arrested with drugs at an Indonesian airport passed through security screening at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) without his baggage being flagged, according to The Star . Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said checks confirmed that the pilot underwent all required screening before boarding the aircraft on July 28. Mohd Shuhaily said the screening system combined artificial intelligence with human assessment, with the scanner assigning a risk level to baggage before security personnel decided whether further inspection was required.

items.title: Defence claims celebrity preacher Da’i Syed conviction unsafe, insists victim’s actions pointed to consent
items.summary: Lawyer Datuk M M Athimulan, representing Da’i Syed, submitted that the prosecution’s own evidence disclosed numerous circumstances indicating that the sexual intercourse between the appellant and the victim was consensual. Athimulan said the Sessions Court had subsequently acquitted and discharged Da’i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, at the close of the prosecution’s case without calling for his defence. The appellant was later convicted by another Sessions Court judge.
